title: ack_always::Sender has hardcoded MAX_PACKET_SIZE instead of using caller storage
description:
The ack_always::Sender embeds a 1280-byte internal buffer, forcing stack allocation and limiting packet size, while NoAckSender and AckOnErrorSender take caller-provided storage.

**Location:** /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/ack_always.rs:16-17,54

```rust
const MAX_PACKET_SIZE: usize = 1280;
...
packet: [u8; MAX_PACKET_SIZE],
```

**What goes wrong:**
1. Stack bloat: Each Sender instance consumes 1280 bytes on the stack regardless of actual packet size
2. Inconsistent API: NoAckSender takes &'a [u8] (borrows caller data); AckOnErrorSender takes &'a [u8]; but ack_always::Sender copies into internal buffer
3. Fixed limit: Cannot fragment packets larger than 1280 bytes even if caller has more memory
4. No-std unfriendly: 1280 bytes may exceed embedded stack limits

**Fix:** Change to match the other senders - take `&'a [u8]` payload reference instead of copying:
```rust
pub struct Sender<'a, const M: u8, const N: u8, const T: u8, const TILE: usize> {
    payload: &'a [u8],
    ...
}
```

This is a breaking change but aligns the API across all fragmentation modes.
close_reason: Updated ack_always API to follow ack_on_error borrowed storage pattern
